name: Hoi An & Da Nang
tagline: Lantern-lit heritage town beside Da Nang's golden coast.
whenBlurb: February to May is dry and pleasant, with the lantern festival glowing on every full moon; October and November bring the wettest months and real flood risk.

ourTake.lede: Treat Hoi An and Da Nang as one trip with two moods, the old town for lantern-lit evenings and tailors, Da Nang and its beaches for space, seafood and a proper resort base. See the old town at dawn or after the day-trippers leave; in the middle of the day it's a crush. The Marble Mountains and My Son are the day-trips that actually earn the drive, and the beach between the two cities is where you should be sleeping.
ourTake.comeIf: You want a lantern-lit old town, a nearby beach and tailoring and food that stay with you.
ourTake.skipIf: You want a city buzz or nightlife; Hoi An is romantic, gentle and slow by nature.

heading.text: Hoi An & Da Nang, in hand.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Four Seasons Resort The Nam Hai, Hoi An
items.area: Hoi An, Ha My Beach (between Hoi An town and Da Nang)
credentials: MICHELIN Two Keys (2025)
Forbes Travel Guide Five-Star (2026, eighth consecutive year)
Travel + Leisure T+L 500 World's Best Hotels (2025)
items.description: The coast's defining address, palatial pool villas laid out to a feng-shui grid along a kilometre of private beach.

items.name: InterContinental Danang Sun Peninsula Resort
credentials: Designed by Bill Bensley, an acknowledged design icon
Home to La Maison 1888, MICHELIN One Star (2026), Central Vietnam's only star
Travel + Leisure, Best Island & Beach Resort in Vietnam (2025)
Condé Nast Traveler, Best Hotel in Vietnam (2025)
World Travel Awards, Asia's Leading Luxury Resort (2025)
items.description: Bill Bensley's tiered fantasy tumbling down a jungle peninsula on its own funicular, the most theatrical resort in Vietnam.

items.name: Banyan Tree Lang Co
items.area: Lang Co, Lang Co Bay (≈60 km north of Hoi An, near Hue)
credentials: MICHELIN Two Keys (2025)
MICHELIN Guide Hotel (Vietnam selection)
items.description: All-pool-villa calm on a sweeping bay between mountain and sea, a golf course, a spa and real seclusion.

items.name: Anantara Hoi An Resort
items.area: Hoi An, Thu Bon riverside, edge of the Ancient Town
credentials: MICHELIN Guide Hotel (Hoi An selection)
Travel + Leisure, Best Suburban Hotel in Vietnam (2025)
items.description: Colonial-style rooms in riverside gardens, a short walk from the lantern-lit old town, the best address actually in Hoi An.

items.name: TIA Wellness Resort
items.area: Da Nang, My Khe / My An Beach
credentials: Condé Nast Traveler, Luxury Spa Award (2021)
A pioneer of the spa-inclusive resort model (formerly Fusion Maia)
items.description: An all-spa-inclusive beach retreat, every stay includes daily treatments and quiet, plant-leaning cooking.

items.name: Hyatt Regency Danang Resort & Spa
items.area: Da Nang, Non Nuoc Beach (below the Marble Mountains)
credentials: MICHELIN Guide Hotel (Da Nang selection)
items.description: A big, well-run beachfront resort on a broad strand, reliable international polish, pools to the sea and space for everyone.

items.name: New World Hoiana Hotel
items.area: Hoi An, Hoiana, Duy Hai (south of Hoi An town)
credentials: Forbes Travel Guide Four-Star (2025)
items.description: A serene, contemporary beach hotel within the Hoiana integrated resort, long private sand, quiet by design, adults-only calm.

items.name: Hoi An Ancient Town
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Hoi An Ancient Town (inscribed 1999)
items.description: The heart of everything, a perfectly preserved 15th-to-19th-century trading port of ochre-washed merchant houses, wooden shopfronts and narrow lanes strung with silk lanterns, closed to cars and best walked at dusk when the whole town glows. Buy a single Old Town ticket at the official booths (it covers five heritage sites of your choice) and let a private guide unspool the story of the Vietnamese, Chinese and Japanese traders who built it.

items.name: Japanese Covered Bridge (Chua Cau)
credentials: Featured on Vietnam's 20,000-dong banknote
items.description: The single most photographed image of Hoi An, an 18-metre roofed wooden bridge built by the Japanese community in the 17th century, guarded by carved dogs and monkeys, linking the old Japanese and Chinese quarters over a narrow canal. It appears on Vietnam's 20,000-dong note; come early morning before the crowds for the reflection in the still water.

items.name: Fujian Assembly Hall (Phuc Kien / Phuoc Kien)
items.description: The grandest of Hoi An's Chinese congregation halls, a riot of dragons, a triple gate, coiled incense spirals hanging from the rafters and an altar to Thien Hau, the sea goddess who protected Fujian merchants on the voyage south. The mosaic-and-ceramic courtyard is spectacular, and the whole complex reads to Indian visitors as a temple-cum-clubhouse of a diaspora far from home.

items.name: Cantonese Assembly Hall (Quang Trieu)
items.description: A serene 19th-century hall at 176 Tran Phu, built by Cantonese traders and dedicated to Quan Cong, the red-faced god of loyalty and good fortune in business. The carved stone-and-wood detailing and the ornamental dragon fountain in the rear garden make it a quieter, more contemplative stop than the Fujian hall.

items.name: Tan Ky Old House
items.description: The best-preserved merchant home in town, more than 200 years old, a jewel-box of Vietnamese, Chinese and Japanese carpentry with mother-of-pearl calligraphy inlays, a lattice-lit courtyard and beams that survive because they were built to flex, not fight, the annual floods. Still owned by the seventh generation of the family; a guide brings the trader's daily life vividly to life.

items.name: Phung Hung Old House
items.description: One of the oldest houses in Hoi An, nearly 250 years old and held by the same family for eight generations, once a shop trading cinnamon, pepper, silk and glassware. Its two-storey wooden structure with a Japanese-style roof and a trapdoor to hoist goods above the floods is the clearest window into how a wealthy merchant clan actually lived.

items.name: Duc An Old House
items.description: A handsome old house that was, at the turn of the last century, a bookshop and gathering place for reformers, the ideas exchanged here helped seed Vietnam's revolutionary movement against French rule. Layered with history and still lived in by descendants, it rewards travellers who like their heritage with a story rather than just a facade.

items.name: Museum of Trade Ceramics
items.description: Set in a restored two-storey wooden house on Tran Phu, this small museum tells the story of the porcelain and stoneware that flowed through Hoi An's port between the Chinese, Japanese, Arab and European trade routes, including shards recovered from shipwrecks off the coast. A quiet, beautifully mounted stop that anchors why the town existed at all.

items.name: Precious Heritage Art Gallery Museum (Rehahn)
items.description: French photographer Rehahn's decade-long portrait project of Vietnam's 54 ethnic groups, displayed with the real costumes he collected across the country in a beautiful heritage house, free to enter, no Old Town ticket needed. Genuinely moving for multi-generational groups, and one of the most quietly powerful cultural experiences in town.

items.name: Hoi An Central Market
items.description: The town's working heart on the riverfront, pyramids of herbs, chillies and fresh produce, the fabric halls where tailors source silk, and a food court famous for cao lau noodles and white rose dumplings. Go with a private guide early in the day, before the heat, for the market at its most alive; wonderful for a veg-loving family reading the piles of Vietnamese greens.

items.name: Riverfront lantern walk & full-moon lantern festival
items.description: On the evening of the 14th day of each lunar month the town cuts its electric lights and glows only by silk lantern and candle, with the riverbank alive from around 6pm to 10pm, this is the Hoi An most people come for. Even on ordinary nights the lantern-lit riverfront is pure romance; time a visit around the full moon and let the family float a candle downstream.

items.name: Thu Bon River boat & floating-lantern ride
items.description: A short row out onto the Thu Bon at dusk in a small wooden sampan, releasing paper lotus lanterns onto the black water while the lit town drifts past, quietly magical, and a highlight for children and grandparents alike. Charter a private boat rather than joining a shared one so the family has the river and the moment to itself.

items.name: An Hoi Night Market
items.description: Cross the footbridge to An Hoi islet for the nightly market, a tunnel of hundreds of glowing silk lanterns for sale, street-food stalls and souvenir stands humming until late. Touristy but genuinely pretty, and the single best place to buy the collapsible silk lanterns to carry home.

items.name: Bespoke tailoring
items.description: Hoi An is Asia's tailoring capital, hundreds of shops will cut a made-to-measure suit, dress or coat in 24 to 48 hours, and the best houses (Yaly, A Dong Silk, Bebe) do genuinely fine work with a fitting or two. A wardrobe made to your own patterns is the quintessential Hoi An souvenir; a good concierge will book the top atelier and manage the fittings around your days.

items.name: Hoi An Silk Village
items.description: A living workshop on the edge of town where you can watch the whole journey from mulberry leaf to silkworm cocoon to hand-woven loom, see the rare Cham brocade technique, and understand the fabric your tailored clothes are cut from. A gentle, educational hour that adds real depth to the shopping.

items.name: Leather & shoemaking
items.description: Alongside the tailors, Hoi An's cobblers will make bespoke leather shoes, boots, bags and belts to your own design in a day or two, at a fraction of European prices. Bring a photo of what you want; the better workshops copy and customise beautifully.

items.name: Tra Que Vegetable Village
items.description: A centuries-old organic herb-and-vegetable village a few kilometres from town, where farmers still tend beds of mint, basil, coriander and lettuce by hand and fertilise with lake weed from the adjacent lagoon. A dream for a vegetarian family, you can walk the fragrant beds, try your hand at hoeing and watering, and then eat what grows there. The natural home of a great cooking class.

items.name: Tra Que cooking class
items.description: The finest vegetarian-friendly cooking experience in Hoi An, pick your own herbs in the organic gardens, learn to fold fresh spring rolls, banana-flower salad and Hoi An pancakes, and eat by the water. Central Vietnamese cooking leans hard on fresh greens and rice, so a veg-first Indian family eats gloriously well here.

items.name: Cam Thanh basket-boat ride (coconut-palm village)
items.description: Southeast of town, the Bay Mau nipa-palm water forest is threaded with canals you explore in a round bamboo basket boat, spinning demonstrations, crab-catching and coconut-leaf weaving make it a joyful, hands-on hour for children and grandparents. Charter a private boat and go mid-morning, before the day-tour crowds and the loud music of the busier operators.

items.name: Countryside & rice-paddy bicycle ride
items.description: The land just beyond the Old Town is flat, green and laced with paddy fields, water buffalo and village lanes, perfect for a gentle guided cycle at golden hour, past farmers working the rice and out to a quiet cafe or the beach. One of the loveliest, most photogenic ways to feel the rhythm of rural Vietnam.

items.name: Wet-rice farming experience
items.description: For families with children, a hands-in-the-mud session with local farmers, ploughing behind a water buffalo, planting and harvesting rice, then a home-cooked lunch, is a genuine, grounding half-day. Several luxury resorts, including the Four Seasons, curate a private version.

items.name: An Bang Beach
items.description: The best of Hoi An's beaches, a broad sweep of soft sand about 4km from town with a relaxed, stylish strip of beach clubs, seafood shacks and sun-loungers, and calm swimming most of the year. The natural place to slow the pace of a trip; book a beach club daybed and let the family drift between sea and lunch.

items.name: Cua Dai Beach
items.description: The historic beach closest to town, parts have suffered erosion, but the stretches fronting the big resorts remain wide and pretty, and it is a quieter alternative to An Bang for a swim. Best enjoyed from the sun-lounger of a beachfront resort.

items.name: Four Seasons The Nam Hai spa & beach day
items.area: Ha My Beach (between Hoi An & Da Nang)
items.description: The region's benchmark address, a Forbes five-star beachfront resort whose spa villas sit on a lotus pond and whose curated 'hidden gems' excursions (Vespa food tours, artisan workshops, sunset river cruises) are the gold standard of discreet luxury here. Even for non-guests, a spa afternoon or a table at the beach is a serene counterpoint to the town's bustle.

items.name: My Son Sanctuary
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, My Son Sanctuary (inscribed 1999)
items.description: A jungle-clad valley of red-brick Hindu temple towers built by the Champa kingdom between the 4th and 13th centuries to worship Shiva, Vietnam's most important Cham site and a natural draw for Indian travellers, who will recognise the Shiva lingams, Nandi bulls and Sanskrit-lineage iconography. Go at dawn with a private guide to beat the heat and the crowds; the Cham dance show adds context.

items.name: Marble Mountains (Ngu Hanh Son)
items.description: Five marble-and-limestone hills named for the elements, riddled with caves, Buddhist grottoes, pagodas and stone Buddhas carved into the rock, with a lift to the summit and long views to the sea. Thuy Son, the largest, holds the atmospheric Huyen Khong cave with light shafting down onto altars, a highlight for the whole family.

items.name: Am Phu Cave (Hell Cave)
items.description: Inside the Marble Mountains, a dramatic cave staged as a journey through the Buddhist underworld and up toward heaven, sculpted scenes of judgement, a climb into daylight, and a wartime past as a guerrilla hospital. Atmospheric and unexpected; older children love it, though the climb is steep.

items.name: Lady Buddha & Linh Ung Pagoda, Son Tra
items.area: Da Nang / Son Tra Peninsula (~50 min)
items.description: A 67-metre-tall white statue of the Bodhisattva of Compassion gazing out to sea, one of the tallest in Vietnam, set in the serene Linh Ung Pagoda gardens on the forested Son Tra peninsula, with sweeping views over Da Nang bay. A peaceful, uplifting stop that pairs naturally with the Marble Mountains.

items.name: Ba Na Hills & the Golden Bridge
credentials: Cau Vang (Golden Bridge), record-holder for its giant-hands design, opened 2018
items.description: A mountaintop resort reached by one of the world's longest cable cars, crowned by the famous Golden Bridge, a gold ribbon of walkway held aloft by two giant stone hands, floating in the clouds at 1,400 metres. Theme-park in feel (a mock French village, gardens, rides) and best for families with children; go on a clear morning before the mist rolls in.

items.name: Dragon Bridge (Cau Rong)
items.description: A vast golden dragon arching over the Han River that, on weekend nights at 9pm, breathes real fire and water to a delighted crowd, a fun, free evening spectacle if you're staying near Da Nang or driving back late. Pure showmanship, and a hit with children.

items.name: Hai Van Pass
items.description: The spectacular mountain road immortalised on Top Gear, climbing from the coast over a cloud-wreathed spur of the Annamite range with the ocean falling away on one side, best done with a private car and driver so you can stop for photos at the summit gate. A gorgeous half-day if you're pairing Hoi An with a run up toward Hue.

items.name: Cham Islands (Cu Lao Cham)
credentials: UNESCO-designated Cu Lao Cham–Hoi An Biosphere Reserve
items.description: A cluster of green islands about an hour offshore, ringed by clear water, coral reefs and quiet beaches, the region's best snorkelling and diving, plus a village, a market and a marine-protected ecosystem. Charter a private speedboat for the day and swim off an empty cove; note the sea is roughest and often closed in the winter monsoon months.

items.name: Thanh Ha Pottery Village
items.description: A 500-year-old riverside pottery village where families still throw clay on foot-powered wheels, try your hand at the wheel, watch the kilns, and visit the quirky Thanh Ha Terracotta Park with its miniature world-monuments in clay. A hands-on, low-key detour that children enjoy and that shows a craft older than the Old Town itself.

items.name: Kim Bong Carpentry Village
items.description: Across the river on Cam Kim islet, the woodworking village whose master carpenters built and still restore Hoi An's old houses and temples, reached by a short ferry and best woven into a rural bike ride. Watch the artisans carve, and understand the craftsmanship holding the Old Town together.

items.name: Reaching Out Teahouse
items.description: A hushed courtyard teahouse in an old merchant house, run entirely by deaf and mute artisans, you order by wooden block and sip Vietnamese tea and coffee in near-silence, a deliberate, moving pause from the street outside. Its adjoining craft shop sells beautiful handmade goods that support the same social enterprise.

items.name: Hoi An Museum of History & Culture
items.description: Set in a former pagoda, the town's main museum lays out 2,000 years of local history, the Sa Huynh, Cham and trading-port eras, with maps, ceramics and bells that stitch together everything you'll see walking the streets. A useful, compact orientation early in a visit.

items.name: Quan Cong Temple (Ong Pagoda)
items.description: A vivid Chinese temple opposite the market, built in 1653 and dedicated to the warrior-god Quan Cong, guarded by two enormous painted horse statues and thick with incense and offerings from local traders. Small but atmospheric, and a genuine working place of worship rather than a museum.

items.name: Assembly Hall of the Chaozhou Chinese (Trieu Chau)
items.description: The most exquisitely carved of the congregation halls, a 19th-century hall built by traders from Chaozhou, celebrated for the astonishingly fine woodwork and porcelain-inlay panels of its altar. Often overlooked, which is exactly why it rewards the traveller who wants the Old Town without the crowd.

items.name: Lantern-making workshop
items.description: A hands-on hour with a lantern master, bending bamboo frames and stretching silk to make your own Hoi An lantern to carry home, a lovely, tactile activity that spans generations and demystifies the icon of the town. Easy to arrange privately through a good concierge.

items.name: Traditional Art Performance House (Hoi An Lune / folk theatre)
items.description: Short evening shows of Vietnamese folk music, bai choi singing games and traditional dance staged in heritage courtyards give a gentle cultural bookend to a lantern-lit night. The larger 'Memories Show' outdoor spectacle nearby is a grander, sound-and-light take on Hoi An's history for those who want a set-piece evening.

items.name: Vespa or cyclo food tour
items.description: The classic Hoi An evening, riding pillion on a vintage Vespa (or, gentler, a pedalled cyclo) through lanes and market alleys to graze white rose dumplings, cao lau, banh mi and che, with a guide who knows every family kitchen. Fun, social and the tastiest way to understand why Hoi An is one of Vietnam's great food towns.

items.name: La Maison 1888
items.area: Da Nang, InterContinental Danang Sun Peninsula (Son Tra)
credentials: MICHELIN ★ (2026, retained)
MICHELIN ★ (2025, 2024)
items.description: Central Vietnam's only Michelin-starred table, refined French cooking in a Bensley-designed colonial mansion above the sea.

items.name: Nén Danang
credentials: MICHELIN Green Star (2026, retained, Vietnam's first)
MICHELIN Selected (2026)
items.description: Vietnam's first Green Star, chef Summer Le's seasonal tasting menu built on roughly 99% local produce, much from the restaurant's own farm.

items.name: Shamballa
credentials: MICHELIN Bib Gourmand (2025)
items.description: Calm, considered vegetarian cooking with a Tibetan-Himalayan accent, meat-free without compromise.

items.name: Rang Restaurant
credentials: MICHELIN Bib Gourmand (2025)
items.description: A rare Bib-Gourmand Indian kitchen on this coast, familiar comfort, cooked with care, when the family wants a night off Vietnamese.

items.name: Bún Bò Huế Bà Thương
credentials: MICHELIN Bib Gourmand (2025)
items.description: Half a century of Hue-style beef-and-lemongrass noodle soup, fiery, fragrant and exactly right.

items.name: Quê Xưa
credentials: MICHELIN Bib Gourmand (2025)
items.description: Mì Quảng, Central Vietnam's turmeric-noodle signature, cooked with real conviction alongside pork-and-herb plates.

items.name: Bánh Xèo 76
credentials: MICHELIN Bib Gourmand (2025)
items.description: Sizzling turmeric rice-flour pancakes and grilled-pork rolls, wrapped at the table with herbs, a Da Nang street-food rite.

items.name: The Long Bar, Four Seasons The Nam Hai
items.area: Hoi An, Four Seasons The Nam Hai (Ha My Beach)
credentials: Inside the Four Seasons The Nam Hai, a MICHELIN Two-Key, Forbes Five-Star resort (2025–26)
items.description: A serene beachfront bar within the region's benchmark resort, the finest, quietest coastal drink on this stretch.

items.name: La Maison 1888 bar & terrace
credentials: The bar of La Maison 1888, MICHELIN One Star (2026), within a Bill Bensley icon
items.description: An aperitif on the terrace of Central Vietnam's only Michelin-starred house, high on the Bensley-designed peninsula.

items.name: Hoi An Ancient Town riverside bars
items.area: Hoi An, the Thu Bon waterfront (Ancient Town)
credentials: Set within the UNESCO-listed Hoi An Ancient Town (inscribed 1999)
items.description: The lantern-lit lanes and river terraces of the old town after dark, low-key, atmospheric, made for a slow evening drink.

items.name: Sky36
credentials: Da Nang's highest and best-known rooftop bar, atop the Novotel Danang Premier
items.description: Da Nang's best-known rooftop, an open-air perch on the 36th floor over the Han River and the city's lit bridges.

plan.heading: 4 days in Hoi An & Da Nang, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Arrive into Da Nang and settle at the Four Seasons Resort The Nam Hai, whose villas open onto Ha My beach.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Unpack the afternoon slowly, the three-tier pools, the spa's water pavilions over the lotus pond.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at the resort's Cua Dai, a beachside table of Central Vietnamese seafood as the light goes.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: A private early walk through Hoi An's lantern-lit old town before the crowds, the Japanese Covered Bridge, the Tan Ky merchant house.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A bespoke fitting with a trusted tailor for linen and silk, then Vietnamese coffee by the Thu Bon river.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Return after dusk when the lanterns are lit and boats carry candles; dinner at Nu Eatery, small and personal.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Drive to the My Son sanctuary, the brick Cham towers in their jungle valley, early before the heat.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Back to the Nam Hai for a long lunch and an afternoon on the water, a private basket-boat or simply the beach.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: The chef's table or a candle-lit dinner on the sand, arranged privately by the resort.

days.label: Day 4
days.title: Da Nang and the marble hills

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Da Nang's Marble Mountains, the caves and hilltop pagodas, then the Museum of Cham Sculpture, the finest of its kind.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A last swim, then a spa afternoon before the flight.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A farewell dinner in Da Nang at La Maison 1888, the Michelin-recognised French villa at the InterContinental Sun Peninsula.

items.name: Hoi An Old Town
items.description: Lantern-lit, pedestrian and photogenic, but busy by day, best for those who want to step straight into the heritage core.

items.name: An Bang / Ha My Beach
items.description: Quiet sand and low-key resorts a short ride from the old town, the relaxed base for beach mornings and evening trips into town.

items.name: Da Nang (My Khe / Son Tra)
items.description: A modern beach city with big resorts, rooftop bars and an airport, for travellers who want scale, nightlife and a long stretch of sand.

events.name: Da Nang International Fireworks Festival
events.note: International teams compete over successive Saturday nights along the Han River, the region's biggest set-piece event.

events.name: Hue Festival
events.note: A short drive north, the former imperial capital stages a major cultural festival of royal ritual, music and craft.

events.name: Hoi An Lantern Full Moon Festival
events.note: The old town switches off electric lights for silk lanterns and river offerings, held every full moon, not once a year.

events.name: Mid-Autumn Festival
events.note: Hoi An is at its most atmospheric now, with lion dances and lantern-making through the old-town lanes.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Stay on the An Bang or Ha My beach strip for resort calm, ten minutes from the Ancient Town; the town floods briefly in the October-November rainy season, and same-day bespoke tailoring is a local ritual worth a fitting or two.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Fly into Da Nang International (DAD); a private car covers the scenic 45-minute coastal drive south to Hoi An's resorts and Ancient Town.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: A private driver links Da Nang, the beaches and Hoi An; the lantern-lit Ancient Town is pedestrian-only and best explored on foot or by bicycle.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: eSIM (Viettel) works seamlessly across both towns; resort wifi is strong and fast.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: Vietnamese dong (VND); resorts and tailors take cards, but carry cash for Ancient Town shops and markets, and tipping is modest.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: February to May is the sweet spot, warm, dry, calm sea. Avoid October and November above all: central Vietnam's typhoon season can bring days of non-stop rain and street flooding in the old town; summer (Jun-Aug) is dry but can top 40C.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: There is no direct flight; you fly into Da Nang (DAD), Vietjet runs a direct Ahmedabad-Da Nang route, but from Delhi, Mumbai or Bengaluru it is one stop via Hanoi or Ho Chi Minh City, roughly 8-12 hours total. Hoi An has no airport of its own: it is a 40-50 minute private-car transfer south from Da Nang, easily pre-arranged.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No mandatory vaccinations from India; hepatitis A and typhoid sensible. Very safe and relaxed. The real seasonal risk is weather, not crime, heed flood warnings in the Oct-Nov typhoon window. Bottled water only.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Central Vietnamese cooking is vegetable-forward and Hoi An has good vegetarian and Buddhist 'chay' options; Jain-style no-onion-garlic is doable with notice. Dedicated Indian restaurants are thin on the ground here versus Hanoi or Saigon, so a good hotel can arrange Indian on request or you rely on the strong local veg.
